title: Skills Coach Handbook 2026/27
author: P009
summary: The definitive guide for Delcorn skills coaches in 2026/27: caseloads, 12-weekly tripartite reviews, OTJ recording, RAG ratings, escalation, breaks in learning and gateway readiness.

version_history.change: Rewritten for fully remote delivery and Aptiva v5
New RAG thresholds based on OTJ % of expected; AI Academy added
Post-Ofsted updates: employer involvement in reviews, wellbeing check wording
2026/27 edition: apprenticeship units, revised caseload weighting, Copilot guidance for review notes

blocks.p: This handbook sets out what Delcorn expects of every skills coach in the 2026/27 academic year (1 August 2026 – 31 July 2027). It is the single reference point for caseload management, progress reviews, off-the-job (OTJ) training, progress ratings, escalation, breaks in learning and gateway. Where a separate procedure exists (for example the **Progress Review Procedure** or the **At-Risk Learner Escalation Process**) this handbook summarises it and the procedure takes precedence on detail.

We currently support **{{fact:active_learners}}** apprentices on programme through **{{fact:coach_count}}** skills coaches across the AI, Data, Digital, Leadership and People academies. Delivery is fully remote: 1:1 coaching and reviews take place on Microsoft Teams, workshops are live online, and all evidence, OTJ hours and signatures live in **Aptiva**.

blocks.callout: If it isn't in Aptiva, it didn't happen. Funding auditors, Ofsted inspectors and end-point assessors all look at Aptiva first. Record reviews, OTJ and contact the same working day wherever possible, and never later than 3 working days.
blocks.title: The golden rule

blocks.h1: 2. Your role as a skills coach

blocks.p: You are the apprentice's main point of contact with Delcorn for the whole programme. You plan learning against the apprenticeship standard's knowledge, skills and behaviours (KSBs), coach the apprentice to apply them at work, keep the employer actively involved, and make sure the apprentice is safe, well and making progress.

bullets: Hold a 1:1 coaching session with each apprentice at least every 4 weeks (monthly), plus a tripartite progress review at least every 12 weeks.
Keep the individual training plan live: planned OTJ hours, module sequence, Functional Skills and any additional learning support (ALS).
Review and sign off evidence in Aptiva within 10 working days of submission.
Rate every learner Green, Amber or Red at every review using the OTJ-based thresholds in section 6.
Raise safeguarding or Prevent concerns immediately via the safeguarding referral form — never wait for a review.
Prepare apprentices for gateway and end-point assessment (EPA) with mock assessments and a gateway readiness check.

blocks.p: Caseloads are allocated by your delivery manager (Sam Patel for AI, Data and Digital; Laura Chen for Leadership, Project and People). Targets are set per full-time equivalent (FTE) and pro-rated for part-time coaches.

rows: Lower target to allow mentoring of new coaches and quality work
Weighting reflects longer reviews and academic assignments

blocks.p: Capacity is reported as active learners ÷ caseload target. Above 110% your delivery manager must agree a plan to rebalance within 6 weeks. Currently **{{fact:coaches_over_target}}** coaches are above target and the average caseload is **{{fact:avg_caseload}}** learners.

numbered: Monday: open the Aptiva 'My Caseload' view and the Power BI Caseload dashboard; check reviews due in the next 14 days and any overdue.
Book all reviews due in the next 4 weeks with the learner and line manager (send the Teams invite from Aptiva so it links to the record).
Check OTJ logged in the last 4 weeks for every learner; message anyone with no OTJ logged in 14 days.
Clear evidence marking older than 7 days.
Friday: update RAG notes for anyone whose position has changed and flag new Reds to your delivery manager.

blocks.p: Every apprentice must have a formal progress review **at least every 12 weeks**, attended by the apprentice, the coach and the employer (normally the line manager). This is a funding rule as well as good practice: the review is where all three parties agree progress, OTJ, targets and support. The first review is held within 8 weeks of the start date.

kv: At least every 12 weeks; first review within 8 weeks of start
Apprentice, skills coach, employer representative (line manager or mentor)
Microsoft Teams, using the Aptiva review form shared on screen
All three parties e-sign in Aptiva within 10 working days
A review is overdue the day after its 'next review due' date

bullets: Progress against KSBs and the training plan since the last review, with evidence references.
OTJ hours logged versus expected to date, and the resulting RAG rating.
Employer feedback on how the apprentice is applying learning at work.
Wellbeing check, safeguarding and Prevent/British values discussion (use the prompt card).
Functional Skills progress where required.
SMART targets for the next 12 weeks, with owners (apprentice, employer and coach).
Next review date booked before the call ends.

blocks.p: Write the coach summary in plain English so the employer can understand it without jargon. You may use Microsoft 365 Copilot to draft the summary from your Teams meeting transcript, but you must check every statement, remove anything sensitive (health, safeguarding detail) and never paste learner personal data into tools other than Delcorn's licensed Copilot.
As at {{today}}, **{{fact:overdue_reviews}}** on-programme learners have an overdue review. Reducing this is the delivery team's top priority for the autumn term.

OTJ training is learning undertaken during the apprentice's normal paid hours, for the purpose of achieving the apprenticeship, that is not part of their normal duties. Every apprentice has a planned OTJ figure on their training plan (for example 310 hours for AI4 and DA4, 370 hours for OM5 and PP5). Expected OTJ to date is calculated by Aptiva on a straight-line basis from start date to planned end of the practical period.

bullets: Delcorn live workshops and webinars, and watching recordings of them.
1:1 coaching sessions (but **not** the tripartite progress review itself).
Self-directed study on the Aptiva learning modules.
Shadowing, mentoring and work on a stretch project designed to build new KSBs.
Writing assignments, reflective journals and project reports.
Mock assessments and gateway preparation.
Progress reviews and English/maths (Functional Skills) study.
Training to do the current job that is not linked to the standard.
Learning done outside paid working hours (unless time off in lieu is given).
End-point assessment itself.

numbered: Apprentices log OTJ in Aptiva at least weekly using the OTJ log, with date, activity type, duration and a short description linked to KSBs.
Coaches verify OTJ entries at each monthly 1:1; unverified entries older than 8 weeks are flagged to Compliance.
Minimum entry 15 minutes; maximum single entry 7.5 hours (one working day).
Workshop attendance is imported automatically from Teams attendance reports overnight — learners should not log these manually (avoid duplicates).
Any change to planned OTJ hours requires a training plan variation signed by all three parties.

blocks.p: RAG is driven primarily by **OTJ hours logged as a percentage of OTJ expected to date**. Coaches may move a learner one rating worse (never better) on professional judgement — for example missing evidence or a wellbeing concern — and must explain why in the review notes.

rows: Agree catch-up plan with learner and line manager; review again within 6 weeks
At risk of not completing on time
Escalate to delivery manager within 5 working days; follow the At-Risk Learner Escalation Process

blocks.callout: Safeguarding is never a progress escalation. If you are worried about a learner's safety or wellbeing, contact the Designated Safeguarding Lead (Grace Adeyemi) or the Deputy DSL (Megan Taylor) the same day.
blocks.title: Safeguarding first

blocks.p: A break in learning is a planned pause, requested by the apprentice, for reasons such as illness, parental leave, a temporary change of role or caring responsibilities. A BIL pauses funding and the programme clock; it is not a withdrawal. There are currently **{{fact:bil_learners}}** learners on a break in learning.

numbered: Learner (or employer) requests the break; coach holds a conversation to confirm the reason and expected return date.
Coach completes the BIL request form in Aptiva with the last day of learning and evidence of the reason.
Delivery manager approves within 3 working days; Compliance updates the ILR in the next monthly return.
Coach diarises a keep-in-touch call at least every 8 weeks during the break.
On return, coach holds a re-start review and issues a revised training plan with new planned end date, signed by all three parties.
If no contact for 8 weeks after the expected return date, refer to the delivery manager to consider withdrawal.

blocks.p: Gateway is the point where employer, apprentice and Delcorn agree the apprentice is ready for end-point assessment. Use the **Gateway Readiness Checklist** template; the delivery manager signs off every gateway before it is submitted to the EPAO.

bullets: Minimum duration of the practical period completed (at least 12 months, or as set by the standard).
Planned OTJ hours achieved in full (100%) and verified.
All KSBs evidenced and mapped in Aptiva; portfolio or project submission complete.
English and maths requirements met (where applicable) and certificates uploaded.
Mock professional discussion or mock assessment completed with feedback.
Employer confirms readiness in the gateway review and signs the declaration.
EPAO booking requested at least 6 weeks before the intended EPA window.

blocks.p: Every coach is observed at least twice a year by the Quality team or their delivery manager (one progress review, one coaching session or workshop). Grades are Strong, Secure, Developing or Requires improvement. You are expected to complete 30 hours of CPD per year, including the annual safeguarding refresher, Prevent training and one sector-currency activity.

blocks.h1: 11. Using AI responsibly in your coaching

bullets: Use Delcorn's Microsoft 365 Copilot (signed in with your Delcorn account) — never public AI tools — for anything containing learner information.
Good uses: drafting review summaries from transcripts, turning notes into SMART targets, drafting employer emails, summarising caseload reports.
Always check, edit and own the output. Copilot drafts; you decide.
Do not use AI to grade or judge evidence against KSBs.
Follow the AI Acceptable Use Policy owned by the Data Protection Officer.

title: Progress Review Procedure
author: P012
summary: Step-by-step procedure for planning, holding, recording and signing off 12-weekly tripartite progress reviews in Aptiva.

version_history.change: Employer attendance target raised to 90% after Ofsted feedback
Signature chase timescales and Copilot drafting guidance added

blocks.p: This procedure applies to every apprentice on a Delcorn apprenticeship programme and every skills coach. It describes how the tripartite progress review is planned, held, recorded and signed off. It supports the Skills Coach Handbook 2026/27 and the DfE apprenticeship funding rules requirement for regular reviews involving the employer.

kv: At least every 12 weeks (84 days) from the previous review
Within 8 weeks of the apprenticeship start date
90% of reviews attended by the line manager or nominated mentor
Review form completed in Aptiva within 3 working days
All parties signed within 10 working days of the review
Any learner whose 'next review due' date has passed without a completed review

blocks.h2: 3.1 Before the review (at least 10 working days before)

numbered: Coach sends the Teams invite from Aptiva to the apprentice and line manager, using the standard invitation text.
Coach asks the apprentice to update their OTJ log and upload evidence 3 days before.
Coach reviews the Aptiva record: OTJ logged vs expected, KSB coverage, previous targets, attendance at workshops, Functional Skills.
Welcome and wellbeing check (apprentice first, then with employer present).
Review previous targets — met, partly met, not met.
Apprentice presents progress and evidence since the last review.
Employer feedback on application in the workplace.
Agree OTJ position and RAG rating (see Handbook section 6).
Safeguarding, Prevent and British values discussion using the termly prompt card.
Set 3–5 SMART targets with owners and dates.
Confirm the next review date (no more than 12 weeks away) and book it.
Coach completes the Aptiva review form within 3 working days: coach summary, next steps, RAG, wellbeing outcome, employer attendance.
Aptiva sends the form for e-signature to the apprentice and employer automatically.
Day 5: Aptiva sends an automatic reminder to anyone who has not signed.
Day 8: coach sends a personal reminder; day 10: delivery manager is notified of any outstanding signature.
Red ratings are escalated to the delivery manager within 5 working days (At-Risk Learner Escalation Process).

bullets: Lead with progress: what the apprentice has achieved, mapped to KSBs.
State OTJ position as numbers: 'OTJ 226 of 310 hours expected (73%) – Red'.
Be specific about support: who will do what by when.
Keep wellbeing detail factual and minimal; anything sensitive goes through the safeguarding route, not the review form.
Copilot may draft the summary from the meeting transcript; the coach remains accountable for accuracy.

blocks.quote: Strong workplace project underway; employer very positive. OTJ slightly behind plan; agreed protected learning time with line manager on Wednesday afternoons.

blocks.p: Delivery managers monitor review timeliness weekly from the Caseload Report. Quality samples 5% of reviews each term for quality of targets and employer involvement. Review compliance is reported monthly to the COO and quarterly to the Quality & Standards Committee.

title: Off-the-Job Training: A Guide for Employers
author: P013
summary: Plain-English guide for employers and line managers explaining off-the-job training requirements, what counts, how it is recorded and how to support apprentices.

blocks.p: Every apprentice must spend part of their paid working hours on off-the-job (OTJ) training. It is a condition of apprenticeship funding and, more importantly, it is the time that turns a job into a programme of genuine development. Apprentices who get their OTJ time consistently are far more likely to finish on time and achieve a higher grade.

blocks.callout: Your apprentice's training plan shows their planned OTJ hours — for example 310 hours over a 15-month Data Analyst programme, which is around 5 hours per week. Protecting a regular weekly slot is the single most effective thing a line manager can do.
blocks.title: In short

rows: Training outside paid hours (without time off in lieu)
Stretch projects that build new skills
Mandatory company training unrelated to the standard

blocks.p: Apprentices record their OTJ in Aptiva, our e-portfolio, at least weekly. Workshop attendance is recorded automatically. The skills coach checks entries every month, and you will see the OTJ position at every 12-weekly progress review. You can view your apprentices' progress at any time through the Aptiva Employer Portal.

columns: OTJ logged vs expected to date
What we will ask of you
rows: Agree a short catch-up plan with the coach
Meet with the coach and delivery manager to protect time and agree a recovery plan

blocks.h1: What we ask of line managers

numbered: Agree a regular, protected weekly learning slot with your apprentice and put it in both calendars.
Attend the 12-weekly progress review (60 minutes, on Teams). We aim for employer attendance at 90% of reviews.
Give the apprentice real workplace projects that let them practise new skills.
Sign the review record in Aptiva within 10 working days.
Tell the skills coach early about changes — new role, extended leave, redundancy risk or wellbeing concerns.

blocks.h3: Can OTJ be done in one block rather than weekly?

blocks.p: Yes. Some employers prefer a study day every fortnight or a block week. What matters is that the planned total is reached by the end of the practical period and recorded accurately.

blocks.h3: What if peak season means my apprentice can't take time this month?

blocks.p: Talk to the skills coach before it happens. We can re-profile OTJ around busy periods, but we must agree it in writing and the total cannot reduce.

blocks.h3: What happens if OTJ falls too far behind?

blocks.p: The apprentice is rated Red and we will contact you to agree a recovery plan. If OTJ cannot be released, the apprenticeship may need to be paused or ended, which affects your levy investment.
Your apprentice's skills coach is your first point of contact. For anything else, contact the Learning Delivery team at delivery@delcorn.co.uk.

title: At-Risk Learner Escalation Process

summary: Four-stage escalation process for Amber and Red learners, including triggers, owners, timescales and the employer recovery meeting.

blocks.p: To identify learners at risk of not completing early and act quickly and consistently. The withdrawals analysis for 2025/26 showed most learners who withdrew had been Amber or Red at their previous review — the warning signs were visible.

bullets: RAG rating of **Red** (OTJ logged under 78% of expected to date) at any review.

Employer has missed two consecutive progress reviews.
Learner tells the coach they are thinking of leaving the programme or the employer.
Missed two or more live workshops without catching up.

Decision: continue with revised plan, break in learning, programme transfer, or withdrawal

Ask the learner and employer what is getting in the way (workload, role change, wellbeing, confidence).
Agree a protected weekly learning slot and a target OTJ figure for the next 6 weeks.
Identify extra support: catch-up workshop recordings, ALS, Functional Skills, mentoring.

subject: Judith Lewis – protected time for off-the-job training
summary: James Rowe and a Redwood Logistics line manager agree a recovery plan after Data Analyst apprentice Judith Lewis was rated Red for OTJ.

messages.body:
Hi Gareth,

Thanks for joining Judith's progress review this morning. As we discussed, Judith is doing really well on her workplace project — the depot utilisation dashboard is genuinely impressive — but her off-the-job training has fallen behind. She has logged {{sql:SELECT otj_hours_logged FROM learners WHERE learner_id='LRN20533'}} hours against {{sql:SELECT otj_expected_to_date FROM learners WHERE learner_id='LRN20533'}} expected at this point, which puts her below our 78% threshold, so her progress is now rated Red.

Judith mentioned she's been covering the planning desk most Wednesdays since September, which is when she'd normally do her study. Could we agree a protected slot each week again? Around 5 hours a week would get her back on track by the end of January.

I've attached our guide for employers on OTJ in case it's useful for the wider team.

Best wishes,
James

Morning James,

Fair point, and I'm sorry — it's been the run-up to peak and we've been two planners down. Judith has been brilliant covering, which is partly the problem.

I can't give her every Wednesday afternoon until after Christmas, but I could do Tuesday and Thursday mornings (2.5 hours each) from next week. Would that work?

Gareth
Transport Planning Manager, Redwood Logistics

Hi Gareth,

That works well — two 2.5-hour slots gives her the 5 hours a week we need. Could you put them in both your diaries as recurring 'Apprenticeship study' blocks so they're visible to the team?

To help her catch up I'll also point Judith at the recording of the Data Storytelling with Power BI workshop, which links directly to her project. I'll check her OTJ log at our 1:1 on 19 November and we'll aim to move her back to Amber by her next review in January.

Thanks for being so supportive.

James

Hi both,

Thanks for sorting this so quickly. Gareth, please let me know if cover becomes a problem again — we can look at temporary support from the Leeds planning team.

James, could you copy me into the next review invite?

Kind regards,
Elizabeth
Early Careers Manager, Redwood Logistics

Thanks Elizabeth — will do. I've updated Judith's record in Aptiva with the agreed plan (Tuesday and Thursday mornings, review of progress on 19 November) and copied in my delivery manager, Sam Patel, as we do for every Red rating.

Best wishes,
James

subject: Prompting Fundamentals – updates for the revised AI policy
summary: Curriculum developer Nathan Shaw and Head of AI Ben Hartley agree changes to the AI3 Prompting Fundamentals workshop following the revised AI acceptable use policy and Advisory Panel feedback.

messages.body:
Hi Ben,

Following the Advisory Panel and the revised AI Acceptable Use Policy that Liam circulated last week, I've been through the Prompting Fundamentals deck. I think we need three changes before the November cohorts:

1. Slide 8 (responsible use) — align wording with the new policy: approved tools only, human review of anything customer-facing, and a clear 'don't use AI to make decisions about people' rule.
2. Add an activity where learners check their own employer's AI policy (Terence's point from Northgrid).
3. Update the grounding slide to cover Copilot agents and the oversharing risk in SharePoint.

Draft v3.1 is in Workshop Materials. Could you review by Friday?

Thanks,
Nathan

Hi Nathan,

Thanks — all three make sense. A few thoughts:

- On slide 8, let's not quote our internal policy word for word; learners work for 70+ employers with their own rules. Frame it as principles, then 'check your employer's policy'.
- I'd like a short bias-and-accuracy check exercise — Sally at Valemont asked for this. Five minutes, using a deliberately flawed Copilot summary.
- I've copied Liam so he can sanity-check the data protection wording.

If we can have it signed off by 20 November it can go live for the 24 November AI3 cohort.

Ben

Morning both,

Happy to review. Two points: please make clear that Microsoft 365 Copilot only surfaces content the user already has permission to see — that's the most common misconception. And avoid showing any real learner data in demos; use the fictional training dataset.

Liam

Thanks both. v3.2 now includes the principles framing, an employer-policy activity, a five-minute 'spot the error' exercise and Liam's permissions point on the grounding slide. Zara is checking accessibility (alt text and colour contrast) this week. I'll send the final for sign-off on 13 November.

Nathan

title: Coaches – AI & Data
summary: Coaches in the AI and Data academies swap tips on Aptiva OTJ logging, duplicate workshop hours, the overdue reviews push and Copilot review summaries.

messages.text: Morning all ☕ Quick one — anyone else seeing learners' OTJ jump overnight? Two of mine went up by 2.5 hours each for a workshop they also logged manually last week.
Yes! That's the Teams attendance import. Since 14 Oct Aptiva flags the duplicates in amber on the OTJ log — you need to reject the manual entry, not the imported one.
Ah, legend. I've been deleting the wrong one 🙈

Confirming what Fatima said. Imported entries have the little Teams icon and the session ID — always keep those. Reject manual duplicates with reason 'Duplicate – auto-imported'. Compliance can then see why the hours changed.

Reminder: Red learners' overdue reviews need to be booked by Friday. If the line manager can't make it, book with a nominated workplace mentor (new rule from the team meeting) but still get employer sign-off.
Mine are all in except Raymond at Arden Retail — manager's on leave until the 16th. Booked the mentor for the 12th.

For anyone who missed the demo — I'm writing up a Copilot prompt for review summaries. Current version: "Using the transcript of this meeting, draft a progress review summary for [learner] covering KSB progress, OTJ position, employer feedback and 3 SMART targets. Plain English, under 200 words. Leave out any health or personal details."
Tried that on yesterday's review — took 2 mins and I only changed one target. Saved me a good 20 minutes of typing at 6pm 😅
Small reminder from the Functional Skills side: maths and English study does NOT count as OTJ, so please don't let learners log FS sessions in the OTJ log. I've spotted a few this month.
Good shout Emily. Same goes for the progress review itself — doesn't count either.
Question for Kate: if a learner transfers from DT3 to DA4, does their OTJ carry over? Saw one show as zero last week.

It carries over if the transfer is done as a 'programme change' rather than a new enrolment. The zero issue was a bad transfer — fixed now. Raise a FixDesk ticket (category 'Aptiva access / sync') if you see it again.
Great thread, everyone. Fatima — can you pin your prompt in the channel once it's final?
